transcript.content: Hi, I’m glad you came in today. What brings you in?

I can’t stop obsessing over how terrible I look in photos and at events, and it’s making me want to avoid people altogether. My primary care doctor actually referred me to you after I completely broke down during a routine visit because of how overwhelmed I've been feeling about it.
When you avoid people, is it mainly because you feel ashamed of a specific flaw in your appearance, or because you’re afraid people will judge or embarrass you even aside from how you look?

It is completely because of how ashamed I am of my appearance. I just can't stop obsessing over how saggy and crooked my face looks—especially my jawline, neck, and these deep wrinkles under bright lights—and I am constantly convinced everyone else is noticing these flaws and judging me for them.
Do you ever recognize that these appearance concerns might be exaggerated or not really noticeable to other people, or are you completely certain the flaws are obvious and as bad as they seem to you?

Even though my husband and friends tell me they don't see what I'm talking about, I feel deeply convinced they're just being polite. To me, these flaws are completely obvious and terrible, and I can't shake the feeling that everyone else is staring at how saggy and crooked my face looks.

Because of these appearance worries, do you find yourself doing things like repeatedly checking mirrors, comparing yourself with others, seeking reassurance, grooming, or avoiding mirrors? If so, which of these do you do most often?

Yes, I do quite a few of those things. I spend a lot of time standing inches from the mirror adjusting my hair and glasses, and taking selfies just to zoom in on my wrinkles. I also constantly ask my husband and sister for reassurance, asking them over and over if my face looks lopsided or awful.

Are your worries focused only on your face, or do you also spend a lot of time worrying about your body weight or shape? If weight or shape is a big part of it, do you also change your eating or exercise because of those worries?

My worries are entirely focused on my face, specifically my jawline, neck, and how saggy and crooked my features look. I don't worry about my body weight or shape at all, so I haven't changed my eating or exercise habits.

Have you ever sought or seriously considered cosmetic treatments or surgery to fix these facial flaws? If yes, did any treatment or reassurance make you feel better for long, or did the worry quickly come back?

No, I haven't really thought about or considered undergoing cosmetic treatments or surgery to fix these flaws. Up until now, I've just been trying to cope by hiding from cameras and avoiding social events altogether.

final_diagnosis.reason: The patient has a persistent preoccupation with perceived defects in facial appearance that others reportedly do not notice, performs repetitive appearance-related behaviors (mirror checking, taking selfies to inspect wrinkles, reassurance seeking), and has significant social avoidance and distress. The concern is not focused on weight or body shape, making an eating disorder explanation unlikely. This presentation is most consistent with body dysmorphic disorder (ICD-10 F45.2 hypochondriacal disorder category, which includes dysmorphophobia).
